question_text: How did the postal service begin?

options.label: A
options.text: Due to the need for faster communication between businesses.

options.label: B
options.text: Due to the necessity of maintaining communications between different parts of an empire.

options.label: C
options.text: As a hobby for kings and emperors.

options.label: D
options.text: To send gifts to family members.

explanation: The passage states that postal service originated in the necessity of maintaining communications between different parts of an empire.

question_text: What was the advantage of postal service?

options.label: A
options.text: It allowed emperors to collect taxes more efficiently.

options.label: B
options.text: It enabled the king to keep track of the happenings in his empire and the progress of his army.

options.label: C
options.text: It helped in organizing social events.

options.label: D
options.text: It facilitated trade with neighboring countries.

explanation: The passage indicates that the postal service enabled the emperor to keep track of all that was happening.

question_text: How are postal services different today?

options.label: A
options.text: They are slower and less reliable.

options.label: B
options.text: Means of communication have improved greatly, and air, railway, and motor services play an important role.

options.label: C
options.text: They are only available to government officials.

options.label: D
options.text: They are primarily used for sending packages.

explanation: The passage mentions that modern means of communication like air, railway, and motor services have greatly improved the speed and efficiency of postal services.

question_text: What difficulties did the mail runners face?

options.label: A
options.text: Lack of proper training and equipment.

options.label: B
options.text: The mail-runners used to pass through jungles, climb hills, cross rivers, brave wild animals and dacoits.

options.label: C
options.text: Competition from other postal services.

options.label: D
options.text: Bad weather conditions only.

explanation: The passage describes the mail runners facing dangers such as jungles, hills, rivers, wild animals, and dacoits.

question_text: Who was the first person to begin a postal organization?

options.label: A
options.text: Sher Shah.

options.label: B
options.text: Akbar.

options.label: C
options.text: Alauddin Khilji.

options.label: D
options.text: Lord Clive.

explanation: The passage states that Alauddin Khilji had a horse-and-foot postal organization.

question_text: How did Sher Shah promote postal services?

options.label: A
options.text: By introducing airmail services.

options.label: B
options.text: By building a 2000-mile road from Bengal to Sind and constructing sarais along the roads. He also established horse despatches throughout the Empire.

options.label: C
options.text: By using camels for postal transport.

options.label: D
options.text: By hiring more mail runners.

explanation: The passage mentions that Sher Shah built a road and constructed sarais, and established horse despatches.

question_text: Name the two places where the first post offices were built?

options.label: A
options.text: Delhi and Agra.

options.label: B
options.text: Bombay and Madras.

options.label: C
options.text: Calcutta and Bombay.

options.label: D
options.text: Madras and Calcutta.

explanation: The passage states that the East India Company established major post offices at Bombay and Madras.

question_text: What was the use of copper token?

options.label: A
options.text: To identify mail runners.

options.label: B
options.text: To seal letters.

options.label: C
options.text: It facilitated the payment of postage.

options.label: D
options.text: To reward postal employees.

explanation: The passage indicates that a copper token was struck to facilitate the payment of postage.

question_text: According to the passage, what is the main issue with instant food?

options.label: A
options.text: It is too expensive for the average consumer.

options.label: B
options.text: It lacks nutrition and contains more taste enhancers.

options.label: C
options.text: It is difficult to prepare.

options.label: D
options.text: It is only available in limited quantities.

explanation: The passage highlights that instant foods are calorie-packed, contain more taste enhancers, little nutrition, and lack fibre.
